---
title: "Spruce Swamp Elevation Analysis"
format: html
editor: visual
---

```{r}
# ============================================================
# TIDAL SWAMP ELEVATION ANALYSIS
# Present-day MHHW and SLR / Landward Migration Zone scenarios
# ============================================================

library(terra)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. SET PROJECT PATHS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

project_dir <- "G:/Shared drives/Science Program/7. Data/GIS Data/Tidal Swamp Elevation Analyses/SpruceSwamp_Restoration_Elevation-Analysis"

dem_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "data", "dems")
mhhw_file <- file.path(project_dir, "data", "mhhw", "mhhw_navd88_m.tif")
estuary_file <- file.path(
  project_dir,
  "data",
  "OR_Estuary_Boundaries.gpkg"
)

# Update layer name if input is a GeoPackage with multiple layers
estuary_layer <- "Nehalem_River"

lmz_file <- file.path(
  project_dir,
  "data",
  "OR_LMZ_Zones.gpkg"
)

# Update layer name if input is a GeoPackage with multiple layers
lmz_layer <- "0_8_FT"

output_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "outputs")

dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. READ AND MOSAIC DOGAMI DEM TILES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

dem_files <- list.files(
  dem_dir,
  pattern = "\\.(tif|tiff)$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

stopifnot(length(dem_files) > 0)

dem_tiles <- lapply(dem_files, rast)

# Use mean where overlapping DEM cells occur.
# Change fun if DOGAMI documentation recommends another method.
dem_mosaic <- do.call(mosaic, c(dem_tiles, fun = "mean"))

writeRaster(
  dem_mosaic,
  file.path(output_dir, "dem_mosaic_original_units.tif"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. READ MHHW AND PROJECT DATA TO ITS CRS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

mhhw <- rast(mhhw_file)

# Target CRS = NOAA MHHW raster CRS
target_crs <- crs(mhhw)

# Confirm expected projection:
# Expected: NAD83 / UTM zone 10N (EPSG:26910)
crs(mhhw)

# Reproject DEM to MHHW CRS.
# Bilinear interpolation is appropriate for continuous elevation.
dem_utm <- project(dem_mosaic, target_crs, method = "bilinear")

# Read and project the current estuary extent.
estuary <- vect(estuary_file, layer = estuary_layer)
estuary_utm <- project(estuary, target_crs)

# Read and project Landward Migration Zones.
lmz <- vect(lmz_file, layer = lmz_layer)
lmz_utm <- project(lmz, target_crs)


# CLIP LMZ TO THE SELECTED ESTUARY BOUNDARY

# This retains only the portion of LMZ polygons that overlaps
# the selected estuary layer (e.g., "Nehalem").
lmz_estuary <- intersect(lmz_utm, estuary_utm)

if (nrow(lmz_estuary) == 0) {
  stop(
    paste(
      "No LMZ polygons overlap the selected estuary boundary:",
      estuary_layer,
      ". Check the selected estuary layer, CRS, and LMZ coverage."
    )
  )
}

# Optional: save clipped LMZ output for QA and reuse.
writeVector(
  lmz_estuary,
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    paste0(estuary_layer, "_LMZ_clipped_to_estuary.gpkg")
  ),
  layer = paste0(estuary_layer, "_LMZ"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# Optional visual QA
plot(estuary_utm, col = NA, border = "black",
     main = paste("LMZ clipped to", estuary_layer))
plot(lmz_estuary, add = TRUE, col = "lightblue", border = "blue")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. CONVERT DEM TO METERS, IF INPUT DEM IS IN FEET
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Use ONE of the next two lines.
# If DEM is already in meters:
dem_m <- dem_utm

# If DEM is in US survey feet, COMMENT OUT the prior line
# and UNCOMMENT the next line:
# dem_m <- dem_utm * 0.3048006096

names(dem_m) <- "dem_m_navd88"

writeRaster(
  dem_m,
  file.path(output_dir, "dem_m_navd88.tif"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. ALIGN MHHW TO DEM GRID
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Resample MHHW to match DEM resolution, extent, origin, and alignment.
# The DEM should have 0.914-m cells after processing.
mhhw_aligned <- resample(mhhw, dem_m, method = "bilinear")

names(mhhw_aligned) <- "mhhw_m_navd88"

writeRaster(
  mhhw_aligned,
  file.path(output_dir, "mhhw_aligned_to_dem.tif"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# Optional QA checks:
compareGeom(dem_m, mhhw_aligned, stopOnError = FALSE)
res(dem_m)
res(mhhw_aligned)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. PRESENT-DAY: CALCULATE ELEVATION RELATIVE TO MHHW
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Positive values = elevation above MHHW.
# Negative values = elevation at/below MHHW.
dem_minus_mhhw <- dem_m - mhhw_aligned
names(dem_minus_mhhw) <- "elevation_above_mhhw_m"

writeRaster(
  dem_minus_mhhw,
  file.path(output_dir, "dem_minus_mhhw_m.tif"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# Limit current-condition analysis to the present estuary extent.
dem_minus_mhhw_estuary <- mask(
  crop(dem_minus_mhhw, estuary_utm),
  estuary_utm
)

writeRaster(
  dem_minus_mhhw_estuary,
  file.path(output_dir, "dem_minus_mhhw_estuary_m.tif"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. PRESENT-DAY: RECLASSIFY ELEVATION ZONES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Classes use meters above MHHW:
#   1 = 0–10 cm
#   2 = >10–20 cm
#   3 = >20–30 cm
#   4 = >30–40 cm
#   5 = >40 cm
#
# Values below 0 m remain NA.
#
# The third column is the new class value.
present_rcl <- matrix(
  c(
    0.00, 0.10, 1,
    0.10, 0.20, 2,
    0.20, 0.30, 3,
    0.30, 0.40, 4,
    0.40, Inf,  5
  ),
  ncol = 3,
  byrow = TRUE
)

present_classes <- classify(
  dem_minus_mhhw_estuary,
  rcl = present_rcl,
  others = NA,
  right = TRUE,
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

names(present_classes) <- "mhhw_elevation_class"

# Attach readable class labels.
levels(present_classes) <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  elevation_class = c(
    "0-10 cm above MHHW",
    ">10-20 cm above MHHW",
    ">20-30 cm above MHHW",
    ">30-40 cm above MHHW",
    ">40 cm above MHHW"
  )
)

writeRaster(
  present_classes,
  file.path(output_dir, "present_day_mhhw_elevation_classes.tif"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. PRESENT-DAY: CONVERT CLASSES TO POLYGONS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

present_polygons <- as.polygons(
  present_classes,
  values = TRUE,
  dissolve = TRUE,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

present_polygons$scenario <- "Present-day"
present_polygons$slr_m <- 0

writeVector(
  present_polygons,
  file.path(output_dir, "present_day_tidal_swamp_elevation_zones.gpkg"),
  layer = "present_day_zones",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. SLR / LMZ ANALYSIS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Confirm these are meters, not centimeters:
slr_scenarios_m <- c(
  "SLR_0_48m" = 0.48,
  "SLR_0_76m" = 0.76,
  "SLR_1_42m" = 1.42,
  "SLR_2_50m" = 2.50
)

# IMPORTANT:
# Set this to the field in the LMZ polygon layer that identifies
# the applicable SLR scenario.
lmz_scenario_field <- "scenario"

# If every LMZ polygon applies to every scenario, set:
# lmz_scenario_field <- NULL

for (scenario_name in names(slr_scenarios_m)) {
  
  slr_m <- slr_scenarios_m[[scenario_name]]
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9a. Create future MHHW raster
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  future_mhhw <- mhhw_aligned + slr_m
  names(future_mhhw) <- paste0("mhhw_", scenario_name)
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9b. Calculate DEM elevation above future MHHW
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  dem_minus_future_mhhw <- dem_m - future_mhhw
  names(dem_minus_future_mhhw) <- paste0(
    "elevation_above_future_mhhw_",
    scenario_name
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9c. Select matching LMZ polygon(s)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  if (is.null(lmz_scenario_field)) {
    
    lmz_scenario <- lmz_estuary
    
  } else {
    
    lmz_scenario <- lmz_estuary[
      lmz_estuary[[lmz_scenario_field]] == scenario_name,
    ]
    
    if (nrow(lmz_scenario) == 0) {
      warning(
        paste(
          "No LMZ polygon matched",
          scenario_name,
          "- check lmz_scenario_field and field values."
        )
      )
      next
    }
  }
  
  # Extract raster to appropriate Landward Migration Zone.
  future_mhhw_lmz <- mask(
    crop(future_mhhw, lmz_scenario),
    lmz_scenario
  )
  
  dem_minus_future_mhhw_lmz <- mask(
    crop(dem_minus_future_mhhw, lmz_scenario),
    lmz_scenario
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9d. Retain areas at least 20 cm above future MHHW
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  # Cells meeting threshold receive class = 1; all others = NA.
  suitable_lmz <- ifel(
    dem_minus_future_mhhw_lmz >= 0.20,
    1,
    NA
  )
  
  names(suitable_lmz) <- "at_least_20cm_above_future_mhhw"
  
  writeRaster(
    suitable_lmz,
    file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(tolower(scenario_name), "_suitable_20cm_above_mhhw.tif")
    ),
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 9e. Convert suitable raster cells to polygons
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  suitable_lmz_polygons <- as.polygons(
    suitable_lmz,
    values = TRUE,
    dissolve = TRUE,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  
  suitable_lmz_polygons$scenario <- scenario_name
  suitable_lmz_polygons$slr_m <- slr_m
  suitable_lmz_polygons$criterion <- ">= 0.20 m above future MHHW"
  
  writeVector(
    suitable_lmz_polygons,
    file.path(output_dir, "slr_tidal_swamp_suitability.gpkg"),
    layer = tolower(scenario_name),
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. OPTIONAL: VISUAL QA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot(dem_minus_mhhw_estuary,
     main = "Present-Day Elevation Relative to MHHW (m)")
lines(estuary_utm, col = "black")

plot(present_classes,
     main = "Present-Day Tidal Swamp Elevation Zones")
lines(estuary_utm, col = "black")
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. QUICK STATIC MAP PREVIEWS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(3, 3, 3, 5))

plot(dem_m, main = "DEM (m NAVD88)")
lines(estuary_utm, col = "black", lwd = 1)

plot(mhhw_aligned, main = "MHHW raster")
lines(estuary_utm, col = "black", lwd = 1)

plot(dem_minus_mhhw_estuary, main = "Elevation above MHHW (m)")
lines(estuary_utm, col = "black", lwd = 1)

present_cols <- c(
  "#c7e9b4",  # 0-10 cm
  "#7fcdbb",  # 10-20 cm
  "#41b6c4",  # 20-30 cm
  "#2c7fb8",  # 30-40 cm
  "#253494"   # 40+ cm
)

plot(
  present_classes,
  col = present_cols,
  type = "classes",
  main = "Present-day tidal swamp elevation zones"
)
lines(estuary_utm, col = "black", lwd = 1.2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
